# ICU text support

This is the unchanged bounded source closure of ICU 78.3, commit `21d1eb0f306e1141c10931e914dfc038c06121da`, from the [official source archive](https://github.com/unicode-org/icu/releases/download/release-78.3/icu4c-78.3-sources.tgz). The archive SHA-256 is `3a2e7a47604ba702f345878308e6fefeca612ee895cf4a5f222e7955fabfe0c0`. [manifest.json](manifest.json) records every copied file, the runtime and host-tool source lists, the exact data entries, and all content hashes. There are 455 source/header files (9,753,936 bytes). No upstream algorithms or headers are patched.

The engine's [CMake project](../../Servers/Text/Native/CMakeLists.txt) compiles common code with unused conversion, collation, formatting, service, IDNA, file I/O, transliteration and regular-expression facilities disabled. Public common headers and conditional platform headers remain available for native host builds. A small separate host-tool closure builds `e2d_icupkg` from the same pinned release; it includes the spoof data swap routines required by that tool. The tool-only `pkgitems.cpp` translation unit enables parsing of converter headers while the runtime converter implementation remains disabled.

`data/TextBreak78.dat` is an intentional versioned runtime input, not a compiler output checked into the repository. It contains 60 items (4,797,472 bytes): all break rules, break locale resources and dictionaries, normalization data, and the accompanying common support records listed in the manifest. Its SHA-256 is `64e407b570a21a4b740531a14cd95f0cefc46cef3d8224fd09a0dd386fb7016a`. The package uses the ICU `icudt78l` table prefix and little-endian data. Thai, Lao, Khmer, Burmese and CJK dictionary models are retained. LSTM models are not part of this release profile. The exact payload items match the accepted comparison-source data profile; the package is reproduced directly from the official ICU release archive.

Run `python3 tools/update-icu-text.py --check` from the repository root to verify every source, header, license and data hash offline. Run `python3 tools/update-icu-text.py` to download the pinned source archive, validate its inputs, compile the private host packaging tool with CMake/Ninja, and reproduce the byte-identical data. `--archive /path/to/icu4c-78.3-sources.tgz` avoids downloading an already available archive. The updater does not use an installed system ICU or `icupkg`. All host-build outputs are temporary. A version update requires deliberate review of the manifest, build configuration and executable conformance checks.

The runtime is statically linked into the private `libElectron2DTextBreak.so` with exactly eight engine C exports, hidden ICU symbols and an additional `_electron2d` ICU symbol suffix. It has no `libicu*.so` dependency or standard ICU SONAME, so it does not replace the .NET runtime's independent ICU. The data is embedded as `Electron2D.TextBreak.dat`; initialization copies it to aligned process-lifetime native storage before creating iterators. Native compiler outputs belong under `obj`, output and publish directories and are not committed.

The [MSBuild integration](../../../tools/text-native.targets) enables native build/copy by default only when `Electron2DNativePlatform` is Linux (or unspecified) and the effective text RID is `linux-x64` or `linux-arm64`. The project advertises `IsRidAgnostic=false` so the SDK preserves a consuming application’s RID through `ProjectReference` instead of silently rebuilding for the host. An explicit foreign platform disables this default even when a RID-agnostic engine project reference sees a Linux SDK host. Forcing enablement with a foreign platform/RID is rejected before build or copy, including prebuilt/toolchain inputs. It builds native-host Linux x64/arm64 libraries with CMake 3.20+, Ninja and a C++17 compiler, and copies the result through project references into output and publish directories. Only the Linux x64 private backend was built and executed during this integration. Historical framework-dependent host-example publishes with plain `-r linux-x64` and `-r win-x64` verified RID propagation: Linux includes the private library, while Windows excludes it without running CMake. This Windows package check does not establish Windows text execution. Cross-RID builds require an explicit CMake toolchain (`Electron2DTextNativeToolchain`) or matching prebuilt library (`Electron2DTextNativeLibrary`); the CMake target verifies the selected processor. `Electron2DTextNativeEnabled=false` disables native build/copy for consumers that do not use text. Unsupported runtime targets have no implicit native text fallback. Private text backend builds and execution on Windows, macOS, Android, iOS and Web remain unverified. Build against the target platform's required libc/C++ runtime baseline; a locally compiled library inherits its toolchain's baseline.

ICU and the packaged data retain the complete [upstream license](../../../licence/ICUText-LICENSE.txt), including third-party notices for the dictionaries. The independent managed bidi, grapheme, script and casing implementations keep their own provenance and tests.
